content.text: wrt FEDORA_HOME: leave fedora.home undefined in web.xml and rely on environment variable setting as the default behavior.
Changed scope to emphasize focus on installer aspect
Interesting thread on ACM Queue that I think has some relevant thinking:
Disclaimer: I don't agree with anyone or anything in that thread. {grin} Seriously, there are some good points raised there about GUIs, headless installs, etc.

Headless install + configure is an important capability we need to be able to maintain. Of course, having a web UI that lets you make important config decisions interactively is also very nice. I think the key is not to think of those as mutually exclusive goals.

is there a top level ticket which covers this issue? I'm interested in automated deployments of a fedora.war file into my application server using puppet or ansible. is the current 3.6 release capable of doing this (dropping a war file into tomcat/jetty/glassfish and having a standardised configuration location from which it loads from)

removed all customization/configuration from the war file, and placed it into FEDORA_HOME.  This allows a single generic war file to represent the fcrepo server, which can be deployed or upgraded independently from its configuration.  The role of the installer is to setup FEDORA_HOME, as well as define the mapping between the fcrepo server war files the FEDORA_HOME directory.  The fcrepo server war file depends on FEDORA_HOME existing in order to function

This task shall allow the fcrepo war file to self-bootstrap a FEDORA_HOME without the need to explicitly run a separate installer.  This could be achieved by either (a) automatically deploying a default configuration to a known or temporary directory or (b) having some functionality in the war file that effectively fulfills the role of an installer complete with option selection
